patch.value: Public git history embeds a personal author email and blocks release approval

A full reachable-history identity scan found that every current commit stores a personal email in author and often committer metadata. The repository is already public, so fixing the raw history requires a coordinated history rewrite and force update, not a mailmap-only cosmetic change. No token, private-key, local-path, or LAN-address patterns were found by the current scan.

Choose a public noreply identity; rewrite all reachable branches and tags plus audit unreachable objects; independently scan the rewritten object database and working tree; coordinate force updates and invalidate stale clones; verify GitHub, npm provenance, changelog links, and PR refs; document the migration without publishing the removed personal value.
Publishing releases before remediation would preserve personal data in every distributed clone and package provenance link.
